strings.item.hollowmere_key.name: Key to Hollowmere Manor
strings.item.hollowmere_key.description: A heavy iron key with a bow shaped like a wine glass. Hollis says it was 'acquired'. Hollis does not elaborate.
strings.item.study_key.name: Study Key
strings.item.study_key.description: Found in a drawer clearly labelled 'STUDY KEY - DO NOT LOOK HERE'. Security at Hollowmere was a matter of trust.
strings.item.dented_bucket.name: Dented Bucket
strings.item.dented_bucket.description: A tin bucket with a dent in it. Worn on the head, it makes you look ridiculous (-1 Presence) and makes shopkeepers strangely unable to keep track of their stock (+10% shop discount). Nobody knows why this works. It just does.
strings.item.party_hat.name: Percival's Party Hat
strings.item.party_hat.description: A pointed paper hat in four colours, made for a party nobody came to. Wearing it makes you feel, briefly, like the guest of honour. +3 Presence, slowly mends you.
strings.item.rat_crown.name: Crown of the Rat King
strings.item.rat_crown.description: A tiny golden crown, sized for a very large rat. It fits you if you push. +2 Agility, +4% critical chance, -1 Presence because people can tell where it's been.
strings.item.cape_brooding.name: Cape of Eternal Brooding
strings.item.cape_brooding.description: Black velvet, blood-red lining, and a high collar to stare moodily out of. Sparkles faintly in sunlight, which ruins the effect. +2 Presence, 3% life steal.
strings.item.hollowmere_signet.name: Hollowmere Signet
strings.item.hollowmere_signet.description: Sir Percival's own ring, given freely at the end of a very good party. It feels warm, like a hand on your shoulder. +2 Presence, +1 Will, slowly mends you.
strings.item.silver_sword.name: Silver Sword of the Grey
strings.item.silver_sword.description: One of Hollis's two swords. The silver one is for monsters; the steel one is for people. Hollis is unclear which one is for rats. Deals heavy extra damage to spirits.
strings.item.moonlit_jerky.name: Rolf's Moonlit Jerky
strings.item.moonlit_jerky.description: Dried and smoked under a full moon by a werewolf who swears there's no wolf in it. Chewy. Restores stamina quickly for 5 minutes.
strings.item.field_guide.name: Hollis's Field Guide to the Restless Dead
strings.item.field_guide.description: A battered notebook full of ghost lore, card-game scores and one very detailed drawing of a horse.
strings.book.field_guide.text:
HOLLIS'S FIELD GUIDE TO THE RESTLESS DEAD
(abridged. unabridged. Hollis edition.)

Find THREE kinds of evidence. Match them below. Do not guess. Guessing is how you end up on the Lawn.

BANSHEE: Wailing, Cold Spots, Ectoplasm Handprints. Screams. You'll know.

POLTERGEIST: Floating Objects, Spirit Box, Ectoplasm Handprints. Throws things AT you.

WRAITH: Ghost Writing, Spirit Box, Wailing. Talks too much. Through trumpets, mostly.

LINGERING HOST: Cold Spots, Ghost Writing, Floating Objects. Rare. Doesn't throw things - it ARRANGES them. Not angry. Lonely. They don't need killing. They need company. (Killing works too. I'm not your mother.)

MIMIC: All of the evidence, all at once, slightly wrong. If the chest has teeth, it's not a ghost, it's a chest.

NOT GHOSTS (cross these off):
- Bite marks: vampire. Annoying, not evidence.
- Claw marks: werewolf. See above.
- Your own footprints: you. Stop it.

Scribbled in the margin: 'Trout - last seen chapel roof. How.'
strings.enemy.animated_armor.name: Animated Armour
strings.enemy.wailing_footman.name: Wailing Footman
strings.enemy.rat_king.name: The Rat King
strings.enemy.wrathful_host.name: Sir Percival, the Wrathful Host
strings.line.armor.alert: HALT. ARE YOU ON THE GUEST LIST.
strings.line.rat_king.alert: SQUEAK. (You are trespassing in the Royal Larder.)
strings.line.rat_king.death: squeak... (avenge me, my eleven hundred children...)
strings.line.host.alert: If you won't stay for dinner... you will stay FOREVER.
strings.line.host.death: ...it was... a lovely party... wasn't it...
strings.quest.rats.title: Rats. It's Always Rats.
strings.quest.rats.summary: Vaelen has a rat problem, and is deeply, sincerely sorry that your next adventure is a rat problem.
strings.quest.rats.stage0: Clear the rats out of Bellwether's streets.
strings.quest.rats.journal0: Vaelen apologised four times before even mentioning the word 'rats'. They're in the streets, in the grain, in the Records Office filing. Every adventurer's first job, and here I am, several adventures in, doing it anyway.
strings.quest.rats.stage20: The rats came from the south. Follow them to Hollowmere Manor's kitchen (the back door is always open) and deal with whatever's sending them.
strings.quest.rats.journal20: The street rats are dead, but they were all heading somewhere: south, through the gap in the village wall, towards Hollowmere Manor. Something is organising them.
strings.quest.rats.stage40: The Rat King is dead. Tell Vaelen.
strings.quest.rats.journal40: In Hollowmere's kitchen I found the Rat King: a rat the size of a dog, wearing a tiny golden crown, sitting on a throne of stolen bread. I have killed a king. It was a rat. I feel complicated about this.
strings.quest.rats.journal100: Vaelen paid me, thanked me, and then apologised again, for the rats, the cliché, and the fact that there will absolutely be more rats one day. There are always more rats.
strings.quest.haunt.title: The Hollowmere Haunting
strings.quest.haunt.summary: Something haunts Hollowmere Manor, south of Bellwether. Six hunters have gone in. Two came back. One was a horse.
strings.quest.haunt.stage0: Something haunts Hollowmere Manor. Hollis the Grey, the monster hunter by Bellwether's east gate, is offering a contract (and a key). Or try the kitchen door.
strings.quest.haunt.journal0: The sign at Hollowmere's gate says 'You must gather your party before venturing forth', and somebody has written underneath it, 'we tried, nobody came.' The manor is supposedly haunted. A monster hunter in Bellwether has the contract.
strings.quest.haunt.stage10: Investigate Hollowmere Manor. Find at least three kinds of evidence (check Hollis's Field Guide), then tell Hollis what haunts it. Beware of red herrings.
strings.quest.haunt.journal10: Hollis gave me a key, a field guide and a long look. 'Three kinds of evidence. Don't guess. And whatever you do, don't hide in the wardrobe.' The guide lists five kinds of ghost and, helpfully, two things that are not ghosts at all.
strings.quest.haunt.stage20: It's a Lingering Host: Sir Percival Hollowmere. Hollis can banish him, or you could find out what he actually wants. He's in the ballroom.
strings.quest.haunt.journal20: Cold spots, ghost writing, a table that lays itself. Not angry. Lonely. Sir Percival Hollowmere threw the finest parties in the Marches, outlived every guest he ever had, and has been laying the table for ninety years for people who never come. Hollis says he can be banished. I'm not sure he needs to be.
strings.quest.haunt.stage30: Hollis has made the banishing salt. Go to the Hollowmere ballroom and put Sir Percival to rest.
strings.quest.haunt.journal30: I told Hollis to do it his way. The salt is laid, the doors are open, and somewhere in the ballroom the gramophone has stopped skipping. It's playing all the way through now. That can't be good.
strings.quest.haunt.stage100: Completed: Sir Percival was banished. Collect your fee from Hollis.
strings.quest.haunt.journal100: The Wrathful Host is gone. Hollowmere is quiet. The table doesn't lay itself any more. I'm not sure if that's better.
strings.quest.haunt.stage101: Completed: Sir Percival had one last party, and is at peace.
strings.quest.haunt.journal101: Hollowmere's ballroom was full for one night, and Sir Percival danced the last waltz all the way through. When the music stopped he smiled, signed the guest book himself, and was gone. He left me his ring. The table hasn't laid itself since. It doesn't need to.
strings.npc.hunter_hollis.name: Hollis the Grey
strings.npc.hunter_hollis.title: Monster Hunter (Contracts Open)
strings.bark.hollis.3: Fancy a hand of cards? No? ...Hmm.
strings.bark.hollis.4: Seen a horse? Answers to Trout. Usually found somewhere it can't possibly be.
strings.bark.hollis.dry: Rain's stopped. Wind's still howling, though. Wind always howls.
strings.dlg.hollis.greeting:
A broad, scarred man with white hair, cat-yellow eyes and two swords on his back looks you up and down, decides you are probably not a monster, and looks slightly disappointed about it.

"Hmm."
strings.dlg.hollis.who:
"Hollis. Monster hunter. They call me the Grey." He gestures vaguely at his hair. "Not very imaginative, villages."

"I kill monsters for coin. Ghosts, wraiths, the odd drowned thing in a well. Mostly I play cards and look for my horse. Monsters come second. Third, if the cards are good."
strings.dlg.hollis.contract:
Hollis studies you for a long moment. "Six went in. Two came back. One was a horse. Not mine. I asked."

He hands over a heavy iron key and a battered notebook. "Key to the front door. Field guide. Three kinds of evidence, then come back and tell me what it is. Don't guess. Guessers end up on the lawn out front with a funny line on their headstone."

"And whatever happens in there," he adds, "don't hide in the wardrobe. It always looks in the wardrobe."
strings.dlg.hollis.need_evidence:
"Walk the house. Look for what doesn't belong. Cold where it should be warm. Writing nobody wrote. Things moving that shouldn't. Write down three, match them in the guide."

He taps the notebook. "And mind the red herrings. That house has a vampire in the attic and a werewolf in the garden. Neither of them is the ghost. Both of them are going to make a mess of your evidence."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_identify: "I've got my evidence. I know what haunts Hollowmere."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_poltergeist: "A Poltergeist. Things are moving on their own."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_vampire: "It's the vampire. There were bite marks."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_werewolf: "It's the werewolf. There were claw marks."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_host: "A Lingering Host. Cold spots, ghost writing, and the table lays itself."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_trenchcoat: "A vampire and a werewolf, standing on each other's shoulders, in a long coat."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_banshee: "Wrong. A Banshee would've screamed the windows out by now. That wailing's coming from the garden." He sips something. "It's a dog. A very big dog. With opinions. Go and ask it."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_poltergeist: "Wrong. A Poltergeist throws things. At your head. Usually the heaviest thing in the room." He frowns. "Is anything in that house being thrown? Or is it being... tidied?"
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_wraith: "Wrong. A Wraith never shuts up. It'd have talked your ear off through that spirit trumpet. Did it answer you?" He waits. "Hmm. Thought not."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_vampire: "Ashgrave? He bites decanters. Drinks beetroot juice. Writes poetry about being a monster." Hollis shudders slightly. "Harmless. Insufferable. Not a ghost."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_werewolf: "Rolf? The gardener? He knocks with his claws and wipes his feet. Most polite thing on the estate." A pause. "Has no shirts. Not a ghost."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_trenchcoat:
Hollis stares at you for a very long time.

"...No."

Another long pause.

"But I'd pay to see it."
strings.dlg.hollis.right_host:
Hollis puts his cup down, slowly. "A Lingering Host." He nods. "Good. That's right. That's the rare one."

"Sir Percival Hollowmere. Threw parties for sixty years. Outlived every guest. Died at the head of a table laid for twelve, waiting." He looks out at the rain. "A Host isn't angry. It's lonely. It lays the table and waits for company that doesn't come, and it'll do that until the house falls down."

"I can banish him. Salt, silver, an hour's work. That's the contract." He shrugs. "Or you go and talk to him. He's showing himself in the ballroom now you know what he is. Your call. I get paid either way."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_banish: "Do it your way, Hollis. Banish him."
strings.dlg.hollis.banish: "You're sure? Once it's done, it's done. No more parties. No more anything."
strings.dlg.hollis.banish_go:
Hollis hands you a pouch of salt mixed with silver filings. "Spread it at the ballroom doors. He'll come to you. He won't be polite about it."

"Hmm." He looks away. "Make it quick."
strings.dlg.hollis.paid:
Hollis counts out two hundred crowns, then, after a moment, unbuckles the silver sword from his back and holds it out.

"Take it. You've earned it. And I've got another." He looks at the coins. "Funny. Ninety years of waiting for guests, and the last one to visit was us."

"Hmm."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_peace: "Sir Percival's at peace. He had his party."
strings.dlg.hollis.peace:
Hollis hears the whole story without interrupting, which is apparently a first.

"A party. You threw a ghost a party." He counts out the coins. "Hundred and twenty. Less than the banishing fee. I'm docking you for making me feel things."

Then, gruffly, quietly: "Good work. Better than mine would've been."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards:
Hollis's eyes light up for the first time. He produces a deck from nowhere, along with a small folding table, two stools and a candle. "Vaults and Vagrants. Highest hand wins. Losing hand buys the next round. Twenty-five crowns a game."

He shuffles with terrifying speed. "I should warn you. I've been playing this game instead of doing my job for nine years."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards_win:
You lay down your hand. Hollis looks at it. Then at you. Then at his own hand, which is extremely bad.

"Hmm," he says, in an entirely new tone, and pays up. "Again tomorrow. I'll be here. I'm always here. I've a contract I'm meant to be doing, but... cards."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards_lose:
Hollis lays down a hand so good that it might not be from the same deck.

"Hmm," he says, with deep satisfaction. "Don't feel bad. Took me nine years to get this good. Ignored three kings, two plagues and a dragon to do it."
strings.dlg.hollis.horse:
"Trout." Hollis sighs. "Chapel roof, last I heard. Before that, a well. Inside the well. Standing, not swimming. Before that, the top of a church spire in another kingdom."

"I whistle, she appears next to me. Sometimes in the wall. Sometimes upside down." He shrugs. "Good horse, though. Never complains."
strings.dlg.hollis.knee:
"No. Used to be a dungeon delver. Proper adventurer. Tombs, dragons, the lot."

He shifts his weight. "Then I took a crossbow bolt to the... well. It doesn't matter where. Changed careers. Every guard in three kingdoms tells the same story now. Copying me, I reckon."
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_pitch:
Vaelen winces like a man about to deliver bad news at a funeral.

"I'm so sorry. I want you to know that I know. I KNOW." He takes a deep breath. "It's rats."

"I know you've fought skeletons and shades and very probably worse. I know you have a sword with a name. And I'm standing here asking you to go and hit rats, like you're some farm boy on his first day." He wrings his hands. "I'd have given you a dragon if I had one. I don't. I have rats. Everywhere. In the grain, in the streets, in the Records Office filing. Oakhaven is furious. They've eaten Form 27-B."

"Please. I'll pay. And I'll never speak of it again."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_advance: [Persuasion - a sure thing] "I'll need half up front."
strings.dlg.vaelen.advance_ok: Vaelen counts out twenty crowns, then a few more, then takes a few back. "Half up front. Fair. Don't spend it on rat poison, it doesn't work. They've unionised."
strings.dlg.vaelen.advance_fail:
You open your mouth to negotiate. What comes out is: "Actually, I'll pay YOU twenty crowns for the privilege."

Vaelen blinks. You blink. Neither of you knows how it happened. It was a ninety-five percent chance. Somewhere, very far away, a game master is laughing so hard they've fallen off their chair.

"I'm... not going to take your money," Vaelen says kindly. "Do you want to try that again?"
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_pitch_again: "From the top, then," says Vaelen, politely pretending it never happened.
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_status: "Still rats?" Vaelen sighs. "The ones in town keep heading south. Through the gap in the wall, towards that old manor. If something down there is sending them, it's a big something. A royal something. Mind your ankles."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_rats_done: "The Rat King is dead. It was wearing a crown."
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_done:
"A crown?" Vaelen stares at you. "An actual crown? On a rat?"

He pays you, generously, then adds two potions. "For the trauma." Then, quietly: "Thank you. Really. And I'm sorry. And there will be more rats one day. There are always more rats. But that day is not today."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_bucket: [Wearing a bucket on your head] "Good afternoon."
strings.dlg.vaelen.bucket:
Vaelen squints at you. "Why is there a bucket on your head?"

A long pause.

"You know what? I can't see your eyes. I can't see where you're looking. If anything were to walk off my shelves right now, I'd never know who took it." He turns his back, very deliberately, and starts counting candles. "Lovely bucket. Shame if someone left with a couple of tonics."

Two stamina tonics are somehow in your pocket.
strings.npc.vampire_ashgrave.name: Lord Ashgrave
strings.npc.vampire_ashgrave.title: Vampire (Lodger, Upstairs)
strings.bark.ashgrave.1: Do not look at me. I am a monster. ...You can look a little bit.
strings.bark.ashgrave.2: I have been seventeen for three hundred years. It is exhausting.
strings.bark.ashgrave.3: The rain suits me. It matches my soul. And it hides the sparkling.
strings.dlg.ashgrave.greeting:
A pale young man in a long black coat is standing by the window, staring out at the rain with tremendous intensity. A shaft of grey light falls across his cheek, and his skin glitters faintly, like it has been dusted with sugar.

"Do not come any closer," he says, without turning round. "I am dangerous. I am a monster. You should run."

He waits. You don't run. He looks quietly pleased.
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_ghost: "Are you the ghost that haunts this house?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.ghost:
"A ghost? Please." He sweeps his cape. "I am something far darker. I am a creature of the night. A predator. A beast in a man's form."

"I am also a lodger. I rent the master bedroom. Sir Percival charges very reasonable rates and has never once asked about the coffin." He lowers his voice. "The ghost is downstairs. He is very lonely. It is extremely awkward at breakfast."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.decanters:
Ashgrave goes very still. "That was me."

"I do not drink the blood of the living. I am not that kind of monster. I am trying to be better." He gestures at the decanters with a trembling hand. "Beetroot juice. It's the right colour. If I bite through the stopper it feels... authentic."

"Not evidence. Merely shame. Please cross it off."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_why: "Why are you living in a haunted manor?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.why:
"Ninety years ago, Sir Percival invited me to a party." Ashgrave sighs. "I arrived fashionably late. Eighty-nine years late. Everyone else had died of old age."

"So I stayed. To be polite." He stares out of the window. "Also, there is a werewolf in the garden. He thinks I don't know he looks up at this window every night. I do know. I look back. It is very complicated."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.sparkle:
"I do not sparkle." A shaft of light hits him and he glitters like a festival. "I SHIMMER. Ominously."

"In the old stories, vampires burst into flame in daylight. Proper, dignified, tragic flames. I got this." He looks down at his glittering hands. "Three hundred years. Do you know how hard it is to be taken seriously as a creature of the night when you look like a wedding cake?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_team: "Rolf in the garden says you're 'not like other vampires'. You both keep asking who I like better."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team:
Ashgrave turns from the window at last, very dramatically, and nearly trips on his cape.

"You are not like other adventurers," he says, intensely. "I have watched you. You have a... scent. Of road dust and cheap bread and ambition."

"The wolf will tell you he can protect you. The wolf will take his shirt off. The wolf ALWAYS takes his shirt off." He steps closer. "Choose."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_team_sabrino: "Honestly? Team Sabrino. Have you tried the gnocchi?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_ash:
Ashgrave's face does something complicated that might be joy, if joy had been locked in a crypt for three centuries.

"I knew it." He unfastens his cape and drapes it round your shoulders. "Take this. When you wear it, think of me. Brood occasionally. Stare out of windows. And never, ever stand in direct sunlight wearing it. Trust me on that."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_rolf:
"The wolf." Ashgrave turns back to the window. "Of course. The wolf. Everyone always chooses the wolf. He has the warmth. He has the abs. He has a SHIRT budget, apparently."

He sighs, enormously. "Go, then. I shall brood. It is what I do best." A pause. "Tell him I said... nothing. Tell him nothing."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_sabrino:
Ashgrave blinks. "Who is Sabrino?"

You explain. The hat. The fireballs. The gnocchi. Ashgrave listens with growing horror.

"A third option," he whispers. "There was a THIRD OPTION?" He sits down on his coffin. "Three hundred years of brooding, and nobody told me there was a third option."
strings.npc.werewolf_rolf.name: Rolf
strings.npc.werewolf_rolf.title: Werewolf (Head Gardener)
strings.bark.rolf.1: I'm not wearing a shirt because I'm a werewolf. It's practical. ...It's mostly practical.
strings.bark.rolf.2: Moon's out. Nobody's calling. Time for a quick howl.
strings.bark.rolf.3: If you see Ashgrave, don't tell him I asked about him.
strings.dlg.rolf.greeting:
A huge, shaggy man with golden eyes, a heroic jaw and absolutely no shirt is weeding a flowerbed in the pouring rain, very carefully, so as not to hurt the worms.

"Oh! A visitor!" He stands, wipes his hands on his trousers, and tries to look broody and mysterious. He lasts about two seconds before beaming. "Sorry. Hello. I'm Rolf. I'm a werewolf. Don't be scared. I'm mostly gardener."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_howl: "I heard wailing out here. Was that you?"
strings.dlg.rolf.howl:
Rolf goes bright red under the fur. "That was me. Sorry. I howl when I'm sad."

"Full moon comes round, nobody calls, the vampire upstairs doesn't come down, and I just... howl about it. It's a werewolf thing. It's a feelings thing. Mostly a feelings thing." He scuffs a foot. "Did it sound like a ghost? People always think it's a Banshee. I'm not a Banshee. I'm a Rolf."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_claws: "There are claw marks on the kitchen door."
strings.dlg.rolf.claws:
"I knock," says Rolf, sadly. "I knock with my claws, because they're always out after the change, and nobody ever answers, and I knock a bit harder, and..." He holds up enormous hands. "I always wipe my feet, though. Always. Manners cost nothing."

"Not ghost evidence. Just me, being a bit much."
strings.dlg.rolf.shirt:
"Transformation." Rolf gestures at himself. "Every full moon, I change, and the shirt doesn't. I've lost forty-one shirts. Forty-one. Vaelen won't sell me any more. He says it's 'not a sustainable relationship'."

He looks up at an upstairs window. "Ashgrave says it's for attention. It is NOT for attention." He flexes slightly. "Mostly not for attention."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_ghost: "What do you know about the ghost?"
strings.dlg.rolf.ghost:
"Sir Percival? He's lovely." Rolf's face goes soft. "He hired me ninety years ago. Before I was a wolf, even. Every evening he'd lay the table and ask if I'd like to come in for dinner, and I'd say yes, and then I'd get nervous and stay in the garden."

"He's still laying it. Every night. Twelve places." Rolf wipes his eyes with a very large paw. "I should go in, one of these days. I should really go in."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_team_rolf: "Ashgrave asked me to choose between you. I chose you."
strings.dlg.rolf.team_rolf:
Rolf freezes. Then he hugs you, which is a lot like being hugged by a warm, damp bear.

"Nobody ever chooses me! Everyone always picks the pale brooding one!" He lets go and presses a bundle of wrapped jerky into your hands. "Moonlit jerky. My own recipe. There's no wolf in it. I promise. Probably."

Then, more quietly, looking up at the window: "Did he... say anything? About me?"
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_team_other: "Ashgrave asked me to choose between you..."
strings.dlg.rolf.team_other:
Rolf's ears droop. "You chose him. Or the witch. I heard about the witch. Everyone's heard about the witch."

Then he shrugs, enormous shoulders rising and falling, and smiles anyway. "That's all right. Here. Have some jerky anyway. A choice is a choice, but a snack is a snack."
strings.npc.ghost_percival.name: Sir Percival Hollowmere
strings.npc.ghost_percival.title: The Host (Deceased, Still Hosting)
strings.bark.percival.1: Welcome, welcome! Do come in! Is it just you? ...Oh. Just you.
strings.bark.percival.2: Twelve places. I always lay twelve. You never know who might drop in.
strings.bark.percival.peace: What a party. What a party!
strings.dlg.percival.greeting:
The ballroom grows cold, and then, quite suddenly, it is full of candlelight that isn't there. An old man in a velvet coat drifts across the dance floor towards you, beaming, both translucent arms held wide.

"A guest! A guest, at last! Welcome to Hollowmere! Can I take your coat? Can I take your hat? I can't, actually, my hands go straight through things, but it's the thought." He looks past you, hopeful. "Is it just you? Are the others parking the carriage?"
strings.dlg.percival.who:
"The very same! Host of the Year, eleven years running!" He bows so deeply his head goes through the floor for a moment. "Hollowmere was famous for its parties. Three hundred guests. Fireworks. A string quartet. A swan made entirely of jelly."

His smile wobbles. "Then the guests got older. And fewer. And then one year it was just me and the jelly swan. And then it was just me."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_why: "Why are you still here, Sir Percival?"
strings.dlg.percival.why:
He looks around the empty ballroom for a long time.

"I laid the table for my last party. Twelve places. I sent out the invitations. I wound the gramophone. And then I sat at the head of the table and waited." He smiles, very gently. "I'm still waiting. That's all. A host can't leave until the party's over, you see. And it can't be over if it never started."

"If someone came... if enough people came... I think I could finally have the last dance."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_guests: "Sir Percival, your guests are here. All of them. I brought the whole town."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_me: [Persuasion] "I'm here. I'm a guest. That has to count for something."
strings.dlg.percival.me_fail:
Sir Percival smiles at you, so kindly it hurts.

"It counts for a great deal, my dear. More than you know." He looks at the eleven empty chairs. "But a party for one is just... dinner. And I've had ninety years of dinner."

"Perhaps you know some people who could do with a good meal? Lonely ones. They're always the best guests."
strings.dlg.percival.party: The ballroom doors open, and the town walks in.
strings.dlg.percival.party_me:
Sir Percival looks at you for a long, long moment. Then he laughs, a real laugh, warm and surprised.

"You know, you're right. A party is just people who chose to be in the same room. And you chose." He offers you a translucent arm. "Would you do me the honour?"
strings.dlg.percival.thanks:
"Wonderful. Wonderful!" He's fainter now, the colour of morning mist, but beaming. "I don't have long, I think. I wanted to say goodbye properly. A good host always sees his guests to the door."

"Do throw parties. Lots of them. Invite the lonely ones first. They always say no the first time. Ask twice."
strings.story.party.1:
They come up the drive in the rain, under umbrellas and cloaks and one very large hat: everyone you've met, everyone you asked, and a few people who simply heard there was a party at Hollowmere and couldn't believe it.

The ballroom candles light themselves. The gramophone plays the waltz, and for the first time in ninety years, it doesn't skip.
strings.story.party.dinner: Sabrino arrives last, at exactly eight, carrying three pots and a ladle, takes one look at the twelve empty places on the table and declares them a crime against hospitality. Within the hour, every one of them is full, and so is everyone sitting in them.
strings.story.party.baggy: Baggy dances. Badly. Enthusiastically. At one point Baggy dances with a suit of armour that turns out to be ornamental, and then, later, with one that turns out not to be. Nobody is hurt. Everybody cheers.
strings.story.party.pair:
Lord Ashgrave comes down from the master bedroom for the first time in ninety years, and stands awkwardly by the punch bowl, glittering faintly. Rolf comes in from the garden, and for once remembers to put on a shirt.

They stand on opposite sides of the room for most of the evening. Then, during the slow song, somebody, possibly a ghost, gives them both a little push.
strings.story.party.hollis: Hollis sits in the corner with a deck of cards and loses every single hand to Sir Percival, who can see through the backs of them. He doesn't seem to mind. At one point you are fairly sure he smiles.
strings.story.party.small:
It's only the two of you in the great ballroom: you, and a ghost in a velvet coat. The gramophone plays the waltz. You are not a very good dancer. Sir Percival is a terrible one. Neither of you cares.

Somewhere upstairs, a door opens, and you hear the shuffle of a vampire and the pad of a werewolf creeping to the banister to watch. By the second verse, they're humming along.
strings.story.party.end:
At the end of the last waltz, Sir Percival Hollowmere bows to the room, signs his own name in the guest book in a looping, happy hand, and thanks everyone for coming.

Then he takes off his ring, presses it into your palm with fingers that are almost warm, and walks out through the ballroom doors into the morning. He doesn't look back. He doesn't need to.

The table at Hollowmere never lays itself again. It doesn't have to. Somebody is always coming to dinner now.
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_haunt: "Baggy, any thoughts on the Hollowmere haunting?"
strings.dlg.baggy.haunt:
Baggy's eyes light up. "Case number two! A haunted manor! This is the best day of my life. Again."

The notebook comes out. "Detective's rule for ghosts: evidence lies. People lie more. Werewolves and vampires lie the most, mostly about their feelings. So if you find something that LOOKS like evidence, ask whoever might have left it."

"Claw marks? Ask the one with claws. Bite marks? Ask the one with fangs. What's left over is your ghost." Baggy taps the side of a nose. "Elementary. I read that in a pamphlet too."
strings.comp.baggy.zone.hollowmere: A haunted manor in the rain. With a graveyard. On a dark night. I've never felt more like a detective in my life.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.hollowmere_manor: Okay. Okay okay okay. Rules: we don't split up, we don't read anything out loud in Latin, and we don't hide in the wardrobe.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.1: Sorry! Sorry. Got stuck on a door. Doors are the natural enemy of the follower.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.2: I was right behind you, then I was stuck on a barrel for a while. It's fine. We've made our peace.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.3: Did you know you can't walk through a table? I've checked. Several times. Just now.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.4: Found you! I took the scenic route. Through a wall, I think. Don't ask.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.initiative: Roll for initiative! ...Sorry. I've always wanted to say that.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.map: Do you ever feel like someone's watching us? From above? Moving us around a big map, rolling dice to see what happens next?
strings.comp.baggy.idle.manor: That vampire and that werewolf. You can tell, can't you? They should just talk to each other.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.hollis: That monster hunter, Hollis. I asked him for tips and he just said 'Hmm.' I wrote it down. I think it's profound.
strings.bark.clerk.rules: Technically, page 212 of the municipal code says you can file while falling. Don't test it.
strings.bark.marta.quest: An adventurer told me he'd be right back after 'just one more quest'. That was a fortnight ago. His soup's gone cold.
strings.bark.fenwick.respawn: Someone keeps putting the same book back on the same shelf, every morning, in exactly the same spot. I didn't do it. Nobody did it.
strings.bark.scout.chests: Every chest on this road refills itself every few days. Nobody knows who does it. The Ashbound have theories.
strings.bark.aldous.stack: A traveller asked me to bless his sword forty times in a row. I explained the blessings don't stack. He tried anyway.
strings.bark.vaelen.hoard: You're carrying forty swords. FORTY. Where do you even keep them?
strings.tip.1: You can avoid dying by not taking damage.
strings.tip.2: Enemies are considerably less dangerous after they die.
strings.tip.3: The Bureau does not accept death as an excuse for late payment.
strings.tip.4: Hoarding forty swords 'just in case' is a valid lifestyle. Your carry weight disagrees.
strings.tip.5: If a door is locked, the key is usually in the drawer labelled 'KEY - DO NOT LOOK HERE'. Architects are like that.
strings.tip.6: Quick save often. Quick save before talking to anyone. Quick save before quick saving.
strings.tip.7: A natural 20 is not a personality.
strings.tip.8: Splitting the party is a time-honoured tradition. So are funerals.
strings.tip.9: Your companion is not stuck on a door. Your companion is thinking.
strings.tip.10: Mimics can be identified by their teeth, their tongue, and the fact that you are already inside one.
strings.tip.11: Bards can seduce many things. Gravity is not one of them.
strings.tip.12: Quest givers will wait for you forever. They do not eat. They do not sleep. They are always exactly where you left them. Don't think about it too much.
strings.tip.13: Sparkling in sunlight is not a recognised defensive ability.
strings.tip.14: That mannequin in the hall is fine. Don't look at the mannequin.
strings.tip.15: Wolves in this region carry, on average, 0.3 pelts each. Plan your fetch quests accordingly.
strings.tip.16: The real treasure was the friends you made along the way. The other real treasure was in the sealed room.
strings.tip.17: Hiding in the wardrobe has never once worked. It always looks in the wardrobe.
strings.tip.18: If your horse is on the roof, it is not your fault. It is never your fault. It is always the horse.
strings.tip.19: Wearing a bucket on your head may affect how shopkeepers perceive you. And their stock.
strings.tip.20: Ninety-five percent is not one hundred percent. The dice know this. The dice have always known this.
strings.tip.21: When in doubt, eat something. Sabrino insists.
strings.tip.22: Rats. It's always rats. You may as well get good at rats.
